f1041799719ddb6d23d004cb21e8b09a9316d0c3.summary: IBM X-Force IRIS tracks ITG07, which it says most closely aligns with activity other vendors call Chafer or APT39. Over the past nine months ITG07 intruded into transportation-sector organisations, using legacy tools and a custom backdoor that IRIS named TREKX. The report describes credential theft, lateral movement and data exfiltration. IRIS views ITG07 as mainly engaged in surveillance and tracking of individuals. The initial access vector could not be confirmed.

hedges: IRIS links this activity to ITG07 based on its own data sources, and notes each vendor has an overlapping but unique view of threat activity.
ITG07 most closely aligns with activity other vendors report as Chafer or APT39; this is an alignment, not a confirmed identity.
Symantec's analysis describes Chafer as an alleged Iran-based hacking group.
IRIS says the TREKX backdoor is probably custom-built.
The report says Remexi, a malware long reported for this group, was not observed in this activity.
Definitive identification of the initial attack vector was not possible; the listed vectors are possibilities only.
IRIS says ITG07 appears to be primarily engaged in surveillance and tracking of individuals, with attacks likely carried out to gather information.
IRIS assesses it is very likely the transportation industry will continue to be a high-value target.
